instructions: Closed book. For each item: read the stem only and write your solution in stem_only before you read the options. Then choose the answer labels. Use no sources. Set flag to one sentence when you see a second defensible answer or a missing constraint, else null.

items.stem: A company runs an AWS Lambda function that answers product search requests. At the start of every invocation, the handler downloads the same 300 MB reference file from an Amazon S3 bucket, which makes each request slow. The file changes once a week, and the company accepts that an execution environment keeps using an old copy for a few hours. The function serves a steady load of about 20 concurrent requests that does not grow. Every request must be fast, including the first request in each execution environment. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements with the LEAST development effort? (Select TWO.)

options.label: A
options.text: Rebuild the search service as containers on Amazon ECS with AWS Fargate, with tasks that load the file at startup and keep it in memory.

options.label: B
options.text: Move the download out of the handler into the initialization code, so that the download runs once when Lambda prepares each environment.

options.label: C
options.text: Store the reference file in an environment variable of the function, and read the variable at the start of each invocation.

options.label: D
options.text: Cache the file in the /tmp directory from the handler, and download it again only when the file is not in /tmp yet.

options.label: E
options.text: Configure provisioned concurrency of 20 on an alias of the function, and point the callers of the function at that alias.

items.stem: A company runs an order API on Amazon API Gateway. The API invokes an AWS Lambda function that writes each order to a small Amazon RDS for MySQL database. During traffic spikes, so many copies of the function connect at the same time that the database fails. The function must never run more than 50 copies at the same time. Clients must receive the result of each order in the API response, and the clients already retry any request that fails. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.label: A
options.text: Place an Amazon SQS queue between API Gateway and the function, and set the maximum concurrency of the event source mapping to 50.

options.label: B
options.text: Move the code into containers on AWS Fargate behind an Application Load Balancer, with an Amazon ECS service that runs no more than 50 tasks.

options.label: C
options.text: Configure provisioned concurrency of 50 on a published alias of the function, and point the API Gateway integration at that alias.

options.label: D
options.text: Set the reserved concurrency of the function to 50, and keep the API Gateway integration pointed at the function as it is today.

items.stem: A company stores customer uploads in an Amazon S3 bucket. Amazon S3 invokes an AWS Lambda function for each new object. Some uploads are malformed, and the function fails on every attempt to process them. Today, these failed events are retried and then lost. The operations team must keep a record of each failed event, with details about the failed invocation, as an object in a separate S3 bucket. The team must receive each record as soon as possible after the first failure. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead? (Select TWO.)

options.label: A
options.text: Add error handling code to the function that writes each failed event and its error message as an object to the separate S3 bucket.

options.label: B
options.text: Configure an Amazon SQS standard queue as the dead-letter queue of the function, and read the failed events from that queue.

options.label: C
options.text: Configure an on-failure destination for asynchronous invocations of the function, and choose an Amazon SNS FIFO topic as the destination.

options.label: D
options.text: Set the maximum retry attempts in the asynchronous invocation configuration of the function to 0, so that a failed event is not retried.

options.label: E
options.text: Configure an on-failure destination for asynchronous invocations of the function, and choose the separate S3 bucket as the destination.

items.stem: A company processes clickstream records from an Amazon Kinesis data stream with an AWS Lambda function. The event source mapping uses the default settings. However, one malformed record makes the function fail, and processing of that record's shard stops for days while the other shards continue. The company wants to keep the full content of each failed record for later analysis and keep each shard moving. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.label: A
options.text: Configure a dead-letter queue on the function, so that Lambda moves the malformed record to an Amazon SQS queue after its retries end.

options.label: B
options.text: On the event source mapping, turn on bisect batch on function error, set a retry limit, and add an Amazon S3 bucket as the on-failure destination.

options.label: C
options.text: Add code to the function that catches parse errors, writes each malformed record to an Amazon S3 bucket, and returns success for the batch.

options.label: D
options.text: Raise the parallelization factor of the event source mapping, so that other concurrent batches from the same shard move past the malformed record.
